shortDescription: China's offshore oil major China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC) SSE:600938 said on Thursday it had drilled a high-yield oil and gas well in volcanic formations at a depth of more than 5,700 meters (circa 18,700 feet) in the Bohai Sea.

children: China's offshore oil major China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC)
said on Thursday it had drilled a high-yield oil and gas well in volcanic formations at a depth of more than 5,700 meters (circa 18,700 feet) in the Bohai Sea.
CNOOC called the discovery a major breakthrough in offshore ultra-deep gas exploration
The well is located in the central Bohai Sea near the Bozhong Sag, the region's largest hydrocarbon-rich depression
It encountered more than 120 metres of gas-bearing pay zones in volcanic formations and was completed at a depth of 5,770 metres (18,930 feet)
During testing, the well produced about 800,000 cubic meters of natural gas per day

"The success of this well has opened up a new play for offshore ultra-deep natural gas exploration and expanded the scope of deep oil and gas exploration in Bohai," said Xu Changgui, chief scientist and chief geologist of CNOOC
"It is of positive significance for accelerating the ultra-deep exploration process in Bohai and for building a major gas province of one trillion cubic meters in Bohai."
